## 0.8.0 — 2026-11-20
- Quotes and highlights. Start a line with `>` to mark a quote; end it with `@name` (a dash before it is fine) to credit who said it. Wrap words in `==like this==` to highlight them, or start a line with `=` to highlight the whole line. The right rail gets "Quotes" (with the speaker shown as a byline) and "Highlights" sections, and a section only appears when the note has some. Clicking a speaker opens the new Quotes tab under Browse, which lists every quote and highlight across notes and filters by kind, person and topic.
- On the phone: new `>` and `==` keys in Capture and the editor, quotes and highlights shown inline in a note, and a "Pulled out" list under the text.
- Nothing new is stored. Both are read from the text, so older versions show them as plain lines.

## 0.7.1 — 2026-11-19
- Move a single line that has an inline `[[link]]`. The side panel's new "Move a line" list shows each linked line with a button that moves just that line (and the lines indented under it) to the note it names.
- Moving out of the Inbox is now plain: the lines just show up in the other note, with no trace left in the Inbox and no "moved from" header in the target. This covers group moves and single lines.

## 0.7.0 — 2026-11-19
- Edit notes on the phone. Open a note and tap Edit: change the title and the text, with keys for `[]`, `![]`, `!?`, `?`, `*`, `~`, `#`, `@`, `[[` and indent. It saves as you type and syncs to your Mac. The Notes tab also has "+ Braindump" and "+ Scratch" to start a new one.
- Move a line to any note, during or after capture. In Capture, "Any note…" picks any note as the destination (search included). Tap a captured line, or "Move" on it, to send it to another note, whether your Mac has filed it yet or not. Triage now also lists what is in your Inbox note, and each line can be re-marked, tagged or moved to any note.
- Edits made on two devices at once no longer overwrite each other. When a phone edit and a Mac edit were made from different texts, the newer one is kept and the other becomes a note titled "… (other version)".

## 0.6.10 — 2026-11-18
- A new look for Scratch. It has its own purple color: a tinted page, a white card with a colored strip across the top, a purple "Scratch" label, character count and Copy button, and purple scratch rows in the left rail.
- Scratch shows "How Slack shows it" under the card when the draft uses formatting (bold, italic, strike, code, quotes, lists, code blocks), so you can check it before you paste. It fades out in quiet mode until you hover over it.

## 0.6.9 — 2026-11-18
- Scratch: a plain field for drafting something that goes elsewhere, like a Slack message. Press `⌘J` (or "Scratch" in the left rail) to open your latest scratch from the last hour, or start a new one. It opens in quiet mode: everything else fades out, and a pointer on the faded parts brings them back. `⌘J` again returns to the note you were in.
- A scratch is plain text. Markers, `#tags`, `@people` and `[[links]]` are not read, and it never shows up in review, Browse or the right rail. `⌘⇧C` copies it. Clear (`⌘Z` undoes it), Keep as note (becomes a braindump titled from the first line) and Delete are in the footer. Scratches clear themselves 7 days after the last edit.
- Slack formatting: `⌘B` *bold*, `⌘I` _italic_, `⌘⇧X` ~strike~, `⌘E` `code`, `⌘⇧E` code block. Enter continues `- `, `1. ` and `> ` lines.
- `⌘.` turns quiet mode on or off for any note. `Esc` ends it.
- Scratches sync to the phone, where you can read one and copy it.

## 0.6.8 — 2026-11-18
- Fixed the line-height drift that came back when you grouped lines under a `[[Name]]`. Group headers, grouped lines and move traces are now tinted on the line itself, in the same weight and style as the text you type, so the highlight can no longer wrap or space differently from the text box.

## 0.6.7 — 2026-11-18
- A quieter note screen. The header is now the title and a "⋯" menu (pin, copy, type, delete), with one faint line under it: date, who was there, a Not reviewed chip and a Follow up chip. Click Follow up to open the full flag and date controls.
- While you type, the controls fade out and leave only the text, the right rail and the legend. They fade back when you pause or move the mouse. Nothing moves.
- One "+ New" button starts the kind of note you made last. The arrow beside it lists Meeting, Braindump, 1:1 and Journal.
- Sync shows as a small dot when it is healthy. It shows words only when you are signed out, haven't uploaded, or there is a problem.
- Link notes to each other in the middle of a line. Type `[[` anywhere that isn't the start of a line and the same picker opens to choose a note, or to make a new one. Links are tinted in the text, ⌘-click (or ctrl-click) opens one, and the right rail shows Linked notes (where this note points) and Linked from (what points here). A `[[` at the start of a line still groups the lines below it.
- An empty Inbox now says why. It checks sync when you open it, and tells you if this Mac isn't signed in or hasn't uploaded yet.

## 0.6.6 — 2026-11-18
- New Inbox view in the left rail, with a count of what's waiting. Lines captured on your phone, and anything else in the Inbox note, show as a list. File each one into any note from a menu, or delete it. "Open as note" opens the Inbox note itself.
